title: Cross-org compliance burnup and milestone synchronization playbook
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a repeatable playbook and milestone cadence for cross-functional compliance initiatives (SOC2, ISO27001, SSO/SAML, audit log retention) that teams can adopt for synchronized releases and evidence collection.

Scope: milestone definition templates, burnup reporting conventions, owner rotations, automated evidence pull pipelines, rollback gating, and executive rollup for OKRs. This ticket coordinates PM+Eng+Design alignment and delivers the artifacts needed for cycle adoption (dashboards, sprint templates, runbooks).

Why now: Multiple compliance threads are out of sync across teams leading to delayed audits and ad-hoc evidence requests. This playbook reduces firefights, clarifies gating criteria for go/no-go, and produces a single source of truth for auditors and stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: Standard milestone template published to Confluence with clear entry/exit criteria for SOC2 and ISO controls
Burnup dashboard (Looker/Grafana) that rolls up evidence completion by control and team and updates nightly
Owner-rotation calendar and on-call contact list for evidence requests and auditor access
Automation scripts to collect syscall/auditlog retention artifacts and upload to evidence store via secure pipeline
Pilot adoption by infra, runtime, and console teams for next compliance sprint with retrospective notes

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Evidence collection requires manual artifacts from product teams causing delays. Mitigation: prioritize automating log/metric pulls for 60% of controls and include a manual evidence queue for edge cases.

Risk: Conflicting priorities between SOC2 timeline and feature launches. Mitigation: designate a protected assurance sprint week and include product stakeholders in OKR planning to avoid mid-cycle scope creep.
Risk: Auditor access/PII concerns. Mitigation: temporary auditor role with scoped SSO links and audit-only tokens, logged and rotated per-request.
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Use a single burnup view that groups controls by category (identity, data protection, logging) rather than by team — simplifies exec reporting.
Decision: Evidence items have three required metadata fields: control_id, artifact_link, verified_by (name + date).
Trade-off: Full end-to-end automation for every control is impractical this quarter; prioritize 70% automation coverage for high-impact controls (logging, KMS, SSO sessions).
